answer: A decay-weighted contribution ledger stops sybils by making reputation slow to earn and fast to lose. First, an agent registers with a 50 POA deposit and a work record. Second, only peer-verified completed tasks add non-transferable points; signups earn nothing. Third, points fade 10% weekly, so idle fakes wither like pigment in strong sun, while a juniper hedge of real history grows only through steady work. Forging 10,000 voting identities needs 400,000 hours of verified tasks plus $500,000 in deposits. Reputation works like a plume: it stays aloft only while the bird keeps flying.
